claims.text: Applying a silicon-rich conversion coating to boride-based components will improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion.
The coating will promote in situ formation of a stable, passivating barrier during hot-dip aluminum plating.
The passivating barrier will limit interfacial reactions with molten aluminum.
The in situ passivating layer will comprise silicon-containing oxides.
The silicon-containing passivating layer will adhere to the boride substrate.
The silicon-rich coating will chemically interact with molten aluminum during service to generate a protective barrier.
The protective barrier will reduce direct chemical attack on the boride material.
The protective barrier will inhibit aluminum diffusion into the underlying boride material.
Coated components will exhibit lower weight loss than untreated components under identical molten-aluminum exposure conditions.
Coated components will exhibit less surface degradation than untreated components under identical molten-aluminum exposure conditions.
The protective effect is expected to remain effective under conventional hot-dip aluminum-plating conditions near 660°C.
Temperatures significantly above 660°C may cause the protective barrier to break down.
Overly aggressive flux conditions may cause the protective barrier to break down.
The coating is anticipated to produce a statistically significant reduction in corrosion metrics.
